record_scope_reconstruction: Mananga road crossing between South Africa and Eswatini. June 29 customs closure status and July 1 EFF obstruction are distinct canonical observations at the same identified crossing, with no continuous bridge to September permission.

source_checks.finding: Primary SARS notice explicitly names Mananga closed until further notice on June 29; no first onset or cause. Page-level July 2 date does not supply continued closure. Golela notice on same page is separate.

Full relevant contemporaneous report dates EFF closure to Thursday morning July 1. Matsamo traffic and informal routes are separately discussed; do not expand the Mananga event to those routes or to all Eswatini borders.
Original 2015 border table identifies the paired road post and published GPS reference. No historical barrier footprint claimed.

sites.name: Mananga road border post (South Africa–Eswatini)
sites.coordinate_method: GPS coordinates transcribed from Big Game Parks original Suggested Borders 2015 PDF, page 2 border-post table.
sites.precision: Approximately 500 m shared road-crossing area; not an exact historical protest barrier or a merged terminal footprint.
sites.evidence_note: Primary operator visitor table explicitly pairs Mananga with Mananga and gives 25.9331 S, 31.7613 E. Table is reference geography predating the 2021 events; hours there are not applied to the event.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Modal scope: single_site. June 29 port closure observation only; movement cohorts and direction unitemized. Unknown onset and restoration remain unknown; no continuous June–September interval.

onset: The June 29 closure supplies no first onset. The separate protest is reported to begin on the morning of July 1, without an exact hour.

endpoint: Neither Mananga observation dates exact restoration; the September 20 announcement provides later permission only.

scope: Movement exceptions to the June 29 closure status are not supplied.

rationale: The June 29 customs closure notice supplies no cause; the July 1 EFF motive cannot be inherited by that earlier observation.

continuity: Continuity between the June 29 closure status and the July 1 EFF obstruction is unestablished.

New source clarification: Sowetan, July 2, explicitly dates the protest shutdown to Thursday morning, July 1. This resolves its onset day, not its exact hour or end; the earlier June 29 observation remains separate. The September 20 tourism-minister announcement lists Mananga open.
